sections.h2: Where is Monroe and how large is it?
sections.html:
Monroe is the seat and largest city of Ouachita Parish in northeast Louisiana, and the principal city of the second largest metropolitan area in North Louisiana. The 2020 census counted 47,702 residents, which made it the ninth largest city in the state.

The city covers about 31.6 square miles, with 3.7 of those square miles water, and sits at 72 feet above sea level. Ouachita Parish had 160,368 residents in 2020 and borders Union, Morehouse, Richland, Caldwell, Jackson and Lincoln parishes. West Monroe, Sterlington and Richwood are the other municipalities in the parish. The Ouachita River runs through the parish, and Bayou Desiard flows through Monroe itself.

sections.h2: What is the history of Monroe?
sections.html:
Monroe began as a Spanish post. Jean Baptiste Filhiol was sent in 1781 to oversee the Poste du Ouachita, and a fortification named Fort Miro was built in 1791. The town took the name Monroe around 1820 after the steamboat James Monroe arrived.

The Monroe gas field was found in 1916, and the city was once called the natural gas capital of the world. Its population grew about 79 percent between 1920 and 1930. Joseph Biedenharn, the first bottler of Coca-Cola, moved to Monroe in 1913, and his house and gardens now operate as a museum. Crop dusting developed here to fight the boll weevil, and that work is part of the roots of Delta Air Lines.

The older neighborhoods date from these boom decades, and the housing around them shows it. Pre-war houses can have original wiring, plumbing and plaster, which a buyer will want to see inspected.

Parts of Monroe have flooded badly. In March 2016, 15 to 20 inches of rain fell across the area over three days, more than any three-day period recorded there before. In Ouachita Parish about 9,500 homes had flood damage and 5,400 were completely flooded, and crews made more than 1,700 high-water rescues.

If your house took water in 2016, a buyer will want the full story. Gather the repair invoices, the flood insurance paperwork and any elevation certificate. If you repaired it yourself, say so and describe what was replaced.

  • Note how high water rose inside the house and what was removed.
  • Keep photos from before and after the repair.
  • List new drywall, flooring, wiring and mechanical work with dates.
  • Be ready to say whether the house has flooded since.

Monroe also takes severe weather in spring and summer. Thunderstorms with heavy rain, hail, damaging winds and tornadoes occur, and a low-end EF3 tornado struck the community on April 12, 2020 with no deaths or injuries, thanks to advance warning. Roof age and hail history are fair questions from any buyer.

sections.h2: What is the Monroe climate like for a house?
sections.html:
Monroe has a humid subtropical climate. Normal annual rainfall is over 51 inches, and the number of days above 90 degrees averages 91 a year, according to Wikipedia's climate summary.

Winters are mild, with about 35 days a year at or below freezing, and ice or sleet storms are possible. That mix of long heat and occasional ice is hard on air conditioning systems, roofs and exposed pipes. Mean daily highs run about 93 degrees in July and August. The record low is minus 2 degrees. A buyer can reasonably ask when the cooling system was last serviced and whether the pipes in the attic are insulated.

sections.h2: Who are the major employers in Monroe?
sections.html:
The largest employers, from the city's 2019 financial report, are the Ouachita Parish School Board with 2,844 employees, Lumen Technologies with 2,360 and St. Francis Specialty Hospital with 1,584.

Other major employers include Monroe City Schools, Glenwood Regional Medical Center, the City of Monroe, JPMorgan Chase, three Walmart locations, the University of Louisiana at Monroe and Graphic Packaging. Pecanland Mall is the largest mall in North Louisiana. A home near the university, the hospitals or the Lumen offices is within an easy drive of a large employer, and that is worth saying in a conversation with a buyer.

sections.h2: Which school system serves a Monroe house?
sections.html:
Monroe City Schools serves the city limits. It runs three high schools, three junior high schools and 18 elementary schools.

The Ouachita Parish School System is a separate district and does not include any part of the Monroe city limits, though Ouachita Junior High sits inside the city. This split can surprise a buyer who assumes the parish district covers every address with a Monroe mailing address. River Oaks School has a Monroe mailing address but lies outside the city limits. Private options include St. Frederick Catholic High School, Jesus the Good Shepherd School and Our Lady of Fatima Catholic School. Confirm the district for the specific address.

sections.h2: How are Monroe property taxes handled when I sell?
sections.html:
The Ouachita Parish Assessor values property, and the Monroe tax office handles payment questions at 318-324-2536. The assessor's phone is 318-327-1300.

The Ouachita homestead exemption lets up to $7,500 of assessed value, which is $75,000 of market value, escape parish taxes. It does not apply to municipal taxes, and the assessor's millage table says all municipal rates are not eligible for homestead. A Monroe owner therefore sees the exemption on the parish side of the bill and not on the city side. When you sell, the new owner has to apply for his or her own exemption.

The assessor's website offers a Sales Questionnaire for people who recently bought property. It asks for details of the transaction so that assessments follow real prices. If your buyer is asked for those details, the price in your act of sale may influence future assessments on nearby homes.

sections.h2: What does a Monroe sale involve under Louisiana law?
sections.html:
Louisiana requires a transfer of a house to be by authentic act or an act under private signature. Under Civil Code art. 1839, the paper has effect against outside parties only from the time it is filed for registry in the parish where the property is, which for Monroe means Ouachita Parish.

You also have to give the buyer a completed disclosure form by the time of the offer, under R.S. 9:3198. If you hand it over late, the buyer can withdraw within 72 hours, excluding weekends and holidays. If you do not know a fact, the form lets you say so, and an honest mistake that was not willful is protected. For a Monroe house, flood history, roof, foundation and plumbing deserve careful answers.

sections.h2: How do I get around Monroe?
sections.html:
Interstate 20 and U.S. Highways 80 and 165 reach the city, and Louisiana Highway 15 runs through as well. Monroe Regional Airport has three main runways and is served by regional partners of American Airlines and Delta Air Lines.

The Monroe Transit System was created in 1906 as a four-line street railroad and is described as the nation's oldest municipally owned transit system. It now runs 13 fixed bus routes. Four freight railroads pass through, and Greyhound serves the city. Monroe has 17 city parks and the Monroe Civic Center, and the Louisiana Purchase Gardens and Zoo is nearby.

faqs.q: Does the Monroe homestead exemption reduce city tax?
faqs.a: No. The Ouachita Parish Assessor says the exemption applies only to parish taxes, and all municipal millage rates are not eligible.
Monroe City Schools serves addresses inside the city limits. The Ouachita Parish School System is a separate district that does not include any part of the city.

faqs.q: How many Ouachita Parish homes flooded in March 2016?
faqs.a: About 9,500 homes had flood damage and 5,400 were completely flooded, according to Wikipedia.

faqs.q: When is Louisiana property tax due?
faqs.a: It is due by December 31 each year. It becomes delinquent the next day, with interest at one percent per month.

faqs.q: Where is a Monroe act of sale recorded?
faqs.a: It is filed for registry in the parish where the property is located, which is Ouachita Parish for a house in Monroe.

faqs.q: Do I have to tell a buyer about past flood damage?
faqs.a: The Louisiana disclosure form asks what you know about the property, so past flood damage should be reported. The form has to reach the buyer by the time of the offer.
